items.title: One UI 9.5 beta turns still photos into dynamic 3D wallpapers
items.summary:
TL;DR 

The freshly released One UI 9.5 beta for the Galaxy S26 series includes a new Live effect tool for wallpapers. 
 This feature converts a still image into a dynamic 3D wallpaper that automatically adjusts to the device’s movement. 
 First-time users of the Live effect tool in One UI 9.5 will need to install a Spatial Core add-on. 

The One UI 9.5 beta is officially here, and in addition to the features we already know are on board , it also gains a wallpaper customization tool. Galaxy users currently have a handful of ways to modify their lock screen’s appearance. However, the freshly released One UI 9.5 beta release takes things a step further.

A video shared by user S M A Sithick on X reveals a new Live effect option in the lock screen customization page that turns a still image into a dynamic 3D wallpaper with spatial effects. When applied, the wallpaper cleverly adjusts with the phone’s movement, adding more depth and layers to standard photos.

items.title: Tested: Googlebooks are actually great for playing Switch games
items.summary:
Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority 

TL;DR 

It’s possible to run Nintendo Switch games on Googlebooks, including Intel-powered models, via the Eden emulator. 
 This is because the emulator is available in an x86 version for Chromebooks and “certain Intel Atom Android devices.” 
 We can confirm great results when playing Mario Kart 8 Deluxe and Captain Toad’s Treasure Tracker, although Tears of the Kingdom is a tough test. 

Googlebooks have been on the market for just over a month now, and I’ve had a fairly mixed experience when it comes to gaming and emulation on an Intel-powered model. However, it turns out that these laptops actually do a great job when it comes to Nintendo Switch emulation.

The team behind the excellent Eden emulator released an Android x86 version of the emulator 10 months ago, targeting Chrome OS, the FydeOS platform, and “certain Intel Atom Android devices.” This release has largely gone unnoticed by us until now,  so I gave it a go on my Intel-powered ASUS Googlebook 14 (Intel Core Ultra 5 325, 16GB of RAM).
items.t: Tested: Googlebooks are actually great for playing Switch games

items.title: The Galaxy S26 Ultra’s Privacy Display just got a lot more useful with One UI 9.5
items.summary:
TL;DR 

One UI 9.5 lets the Galaxy S26 Ultra’s Privacy Display activate automatically when using specific privacy-sensitive app features, rather than entire apps. 
 The update also extends protection to the notification panel and Recents previews for apps configured to trigger Privacy Display automatically. 
 These improvements are also expected to ship with the rumored Privacy Display-equipped Galaxy S27 Pro and S27 Ultra. 

Samsung’s Privacy Display is one of those Galaxy S26 Ultra features that comes in handy when you’re using your phone in public. Rather than buying a privacy screen protector and living with its drawbacks around the clock, Samsung lets you limit what people around you can see on your screen only when you need to. With One UI 9.5, that protection is becoming more selective.

Currently, Galaxy S26 Ultra owners can configure Privacy Display to automatically activate when they open specific apps, enter their phone’s PIN, pattern, or password, or receive notification pop-ups. You can also switch it on manually through the Quick panel. But not everything inside an app needs to be kept away from curious eyes. You might be perfectly comfortable scrolling through your Gallery in public but feel differently about opening a private album.
items.t: The Galaxy S26 Ultra’s Privacy Display just got a lot more useful with One UI 9.5

items.title: Google Wallet is preparing digital Social Security cards that show your benefits
items.summary:
Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority 

TL;DR 

New code in Google Play Services v26.46.30 reveals that Google Wallet is preparing to support a Social Security Number credential that masks most digits by default. 
 Strings indicate the pass could also track federal benefit programs such as RSDI, SSI, and Medicare, and show Medicare identifiers, status dates, and amounts before and after deductions. 
 It remains unclear if the Social Security Administration is officially involved or if the credential will carry legal weight, as Google has not formally announced the feature. 

Google Wallet has slowly become a place for more than just your credit cards. Its journey as a digital vault has taken in state-issued digital IDs and  passport-based ID passes , and we’ve since spotted Google working on online age verification too. The next government document headed to Google Wallet could be the one most of us keep tucked away in a drawer: the Social Security card.

APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

We found new strings in Google Play Services v26.46.30 that reference a “Social Security Number” credential for Google Wallet. It could carry the basics you’d expect: your name, date of birth, and Social Security Number (SSN). The strings also suggest Wallet would show only the last few digits of your SSN by default, which is a sensible choice for a number this sensitive.
items.t: Google Wallet is preparing digital Social Security cards that show your benefits

items.title: There’s a glaring accessibility gap in Google’s Fitbit ambitions, and it’s time to fix it

From real-time captions and AI-powered vision tools to refined high-contrast display options across Android, the company frequently touts its commitment to creating technology that works for everyone. With the release of its 2026 Fitbit lineup , Google has pushed this mission even further, introducing a suite of features aimed at lowering price barriers, streamlining health tracking, and making health insights simpler to understand.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, but not everyone is sold on the cheaper upgrade
items.summary:
TL;DR 

OpenAI has launched GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, promising improved performance and greater efficiency across professional and everyday tasks. 
 Early testers reported problems with unproductive loops, premature task completion, and confusing responses despite impressive benchmark results. 
 OpenAI believes some reviewers missed last-minute model improvements and acknowledges that there’s still room to improve the user experience. 

Ever since OpenAI introduced GPT-6 Astra in September, much of its attention has been on delivering flagship-level intelligence at a fraction of the cost. We saw this with GPT-6.1 Sol and, more recently, GPT-6.1 Terra . Keeping costs down becomes particularly important as tools like ChatGPT Work take on entire projects rather than simply answering questions. While OpenAI’s latest models push that efficiency even further, some early testers have found that saving on tokens doesn’t necessarily save time.

OpenAI has introduced GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol , with the former becoming its most capable model for complex professional work, scientific research, and engineering. Beyond crunching numbers and writing code, Astra brings improvements that should be immediately visible in the things you create, from more thoughtfully designed websites and polished presentations to richer 3D designs.
items.t: OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, but not everyone is sold on the cheaper upgrade

However, last week, it backtracked and updated the German product page to mention a 7,000 mAh battery, leading everyone to believe German customers would get the same capacity as other regions. Well, a new plot twist suggests that won’t be the case, as Motorola confirmed that Signature 27 will ship with a 5,500 mAh battery in Germany.

items.title: Xiaomi 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max begin their international rollout
items.summary:
Xiaomi hosted an event in Paris, France, today for the international launch of the Xiaomi 18 Pro and Xiaomi 18 Pro Max, which were unveiled in China in September.

The global models of the Xiaomi 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max share the hardware with their Chinese counterparts, except for the battery, which is smaller.

The global Xiaomi 18 Pro packs a 6,000 mAh battery, whereas the Xiaomi 18 Pro Max comes with a 7,050 mAh juice pack. In China, the Xiaomi 18 Pro comes with a 7,000 mAh battery, while the 18 Pro Max is fueled by an 8,500 mAh battery.
